user_question: Compare the top 3 open-source vector databases for a startup building RAG products
short_answer: For a startup building RAG products, the top three open-source vector databases are Qdrant, Milvus, and Chroma. Qdrant provides the best balance of speed, payload filtering, and production ease via its native Rust implementation; Milvus offers superior distributed scalability for massive multi-million vector collections; and Chroma excels in rapid developer onboarding and local prototyping.

key_findings.statement: Qdrant is written in Rust, providing native payload-based filtering, low-latency approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search, and a mature cloud-ready standalone binary.
Milvus architecture is decoupled and cloud-native, separating storage from compute nodes, making it suitable for distributed deployments handling massive billion-scale vector workloads.
Chroma focuses on developer ergonomics with native Python and TypeScript client bindings, fast in-process prototyping, and seamless integration with LangChain and LlamaIndex.
GitHub activity indicates strong community velocity: Qdrant maintains >22k stars and active releases, Milvus maintains >31k stars with enterprise adoption, and Chroma maintains >16k stars.

assumptions: Evaluated specifically through the lens of early-stage startup RAG requirements (latency, operational complexity, ingestion speed).
limitations: Performance benchmarks depend heavily on embedding dimensionality, indexing algorithms (HNSW vs IVF_FLAT), and server memory availability.
next_steps: Benchmark Qdrant and Milvus using a representative sample of company-specific embeddings and query vectors.
Evaluate operational overhead: evaluate whether team expertise aligns better with a single binary (Qdrant) or distributed Kubernetes infrastructure (Milvus).
